questions.question: A bank that has a paid-up capital of ______ and above qualifies for the schedule bank category as listed in the RBI Act 1934.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs 5 lakhs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Scheduled banks are covered under the 2nd Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. To qualify as a scheduled bank, the bank should conform to the following conditions:

__
 
• A bank that has a paid-up capital of Rs. 5 Lakh and above qualifies for the schedule bank category
 
• A bank requires to satisfy the central bank that its affairs are not carried out in a way that causes harm to the interest of the depositors
 
• A bank should be a corporation rather than a sole-proprietorship or partnership firm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Banks are the institutional bodies that accept deposits and grant credit to the entities and play a major role in maintaining the economic stature of a country. 

 
• In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the apex banking institution that regulates the monetary policy in the country.
 
• The banking sector of India can be broadly divided into two major groups’ i.e. scheduled banks and Non-Scheduled Banks.
 
• Banks that have been included in the second schedule of the RBI Act, 1934 are called the scheduled bank while non scheduled banks are not included in the second schedule of the RBI Act,1934.

questions.question: Which among the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vitamin is an organic non-protein substance that is required by an organism for normal metabolic function but cannot be synthesized in sufficient quantity by that organism.
 
• These can be divided into two categories: fat-soluble and water-soluble.

Fat-Soluble vitamins

 
• Fat-soluble vitamins are soluble in fats.
 
• They are absorbed by fat globules that travel through the small intestines and into the general blood circulation within the body.
 
• Unlike water-soluble vitamins, fat-soluble vitamins are stored in the body when they are not in use.
 
• Vitamin A, D, and E K are fat-soluble.

Water-soluble vitamins

 
• Water-soluble vitamins dissolve in water, which means these vitamins and nutrients dissolve quickly in the body.
 
• Unlike fat-soluble vitamins, water-soluble vitamins are carried to the body’s tissues, but the body cannot store them.
 
• Any excess amounts of water-soluble vitamins simply pass through the body
 
• Vitamin B and Vitamin C are water-soluble.​

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Keyboard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The keyboard is an input peripheral of the computer system. It takes the input from the user and sends it to the system.
 
• The keyboard is consisting of letters, numbers and special characters, and functional keys like shift, control, alt, tab, and so on. It has 106 keys.
 
• The keyboard is recognized as a typing device.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word computer is derived from the word compute. In the year 1833, English mechanical engineer Charles Babbage designed the first analytical engine. He is known as the father of the computer.
 
• In the beginning, computers are used for calculating large numbers and can only store a small amount of data.
 
• The software and the hardware parts of the computers are running together to execute the operations smoothly.
 
• Software is a set of instructions or programs given to the computers' hardware to perform a task. For example, system software (OS), application software( MS Office, Browser), and programming software(compiler).
 
• The hardware parts of the computer are tangible parts of the computer which collect the input (e.g. keyboard, mouse, scanner etc.), and process (e.g. C.P.U). It and display it to the respective output devices(e.g. monitor, printer etc.). Sometimes it stores the processed data in the memory.

questions.question: In which layer of atmosphere does the meteorites burn up on entering from the space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesosphere**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Mesosphere:

__
 
• It lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• In this layer, once again, the temperature starts decreasing with the increase in altitude and reaches up to minus 100°C at a height of 80 km.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from space.
 
• The upper limit of the mesosphere is known as mesopause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Stratosphere:

 
• It is the second major strata of air in the atmosphere.
 
• It is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains the ozone layer.
 
• This layer absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the earth from an intense, harmful form of energy.
 
• The air temperature in the stratosphere remains relatively constant up to an altitude of 15 miles (25 km).
 
• Then it increases gradually to up to stratopause. 

Troposphere:

 
• It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• Its average height is 13 km and extends roughly to a height of 8 km near the poles and about 18 km at the equator.
 
• The thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator because heat is transported to great heights by strong convectional currents.
 
• This layer contains dust particles and water vapour.
 
• All changes in climate and weather take place in this layer.
 
• The temperature in this layer decreases at the rate of 1°C for every 165m of height.
 
• This is the most important layer for all biological activity.

​Thermosphere 

 
• It is located between 80 and 400 km above the mesopause.
 
• It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is also known as the ionosphere.
 
• Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• This layer helps in the transmission of radio waves.
 
• The temperature here starts increasing with height.

Exosphere:

 
• It is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• This is the highest layer but very little is known about it.
 
• Whatever contents are there, these are extremely rarefied in this layer, and it gradually merges with outer space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aac671501024a6da0309f9a49fe34b0d0064aba58026951c96927ee90b0dd7a8.png]

questions.question: Which among the following is the official sport of Maharashtra, as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Dahi-Handi**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Maharashtra State officially recognised Dahi Handi as an adventure sport.
 
• The participants, known as Govindas, will be recognised as athletes.
 
• Dahi Handi is an occasion connected to the Hindu festival of Krishna Janmashtami in Maharashtra.
 
• It involves earthen pots filled with yoghurt. In this game, "Govindas" dons colorful clothing and builds a human pyramid to shatter the hanging pot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__****Kalaripayattu:**

 
• Kalaripayattu is a martial art.
 
• It originated in Kerala from the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD.
 
• The place where this martial art is practised is called a 'Kalari'.
 
• It is considered to be among the oldest martial arts still in existence.

Mallakamb:

 
• A Traditional Indian sport, Mallakamb involves a gymnast performing feats with a vertical wooden pole or rope. 
 
• The word, Mallakamb, also refers to the pole used in the sport.
 
• The word ‘Mallakhamb’ comes from coalescing two words- ‘malla’ meaning wrestler and ‘ khamb’ meaning pole.
 
• The gymnast performs aerial yoga postures on a wooden pole, a cane, or simply a rope.
 
• Traditionally, a wooden pole is used to perform yoga postures, which are made of Sheesham or Indian Rosewood and smoothened by castor oil. 
 
• Over the years, three types of mallakhamb variations have gained popularity in competitions.
 
• They are pole mallakhamb, hanging mallakhamb, and rope mallakhamb.
 
• Pole mallakhamb is essentially the traditional form of mallakhamb.
 
• Competitors perform on a wooden pole that is 2.6m in height and has a circumference of 55cm at the base.
 
• The pole gradually tapers to a circumference of 35cm at the top.
 
• Hanging mallakhamb, meanwhile, uses a shorter pole suspended with hooks or chains as the prop.
 
• The bottom of the pole in the hanging mallakhamb doesn’t touch the ground.
 
• Rope mallakhamb is performed on a suspended rope that is 5.5m long and 2cm in diameter.​

questions.question: Who among the following authors wrote "The Living Mountain"?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __Amitav Ghosh__.

__
 
• “The Living Mountain” is a new storybook written during the pandemic by Jnanpith winner and internationally renowned author Amitav Ghosh.
 
• It's a cautionary tale about how humans have systematically manipulated nature, leading to an environmental collapse in our time. 
 
• The Living Mountain will be published as a special standalone edition by HarperCollins Publishers India in January 2022 under its prestigious Fourth Estate imprint.
 
• The book will also be released in Hindi, as well as as an ebook and an audiobook.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

• On November 20, 2016, Ghosh was honored with a lifetime achievement award at Tata Literature Live, the Mumbai LitFest.

questions.question: ______ was the capital city of the Vijaynagar Empire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hampi.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom.
 
• It served as the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century
 
• Hampi was a city located in northern Karnataka.
 
• Hampi is a famous pilgrimage centre of the Hindu and Jain religions.
 
• It is situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.
 
• Hampi-Vijayanagara was considered the world's second-largest medieval-era city after Beijing By 1500 CE.
 
• Group of Monuments at Hampi was added to UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1986.
 
• The site has about 1,600 monuments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Magadha:**

 
• Rajagriha or modern-day Rajgir was the first capital of Magadha.
 
• Pataliputra was a city in ancient India, built by Magadha ruler Udayin in 490 BCE as a small fort near the Ganges river.
 
• Patliputra was the capital of major powers in ancient India, like the Nanda Empire, the Shishunaga Empire, the Maurya Empire, the Gupta Empire, and the Pala Empire.
 
• Patliputra renamed Patna by Sher Shah Suri.
 
• Patliputra became one of the largest cities in the world during the Maurya period.
 
• Magadha was counted as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, and the kingdom was in southern Bihar in ancient India.

**Kanchi:**

 
• The capital city of the Pallavas was Kanchipuram.

 
• The Pallavas emerged as a formidable power in the South around the 4th century AD and were at the height of their power in the seventh century AD.
 
• They were able to sustain their rule for about 500 years.
 
• They built great cities, centres of learning, temples, and sculptures and influenced a large part of Southeast Asia in culture.

questions.question: Part V chapter II of the Indian constitution does not include which of the following provisions?

options.text: Joint sitting of both house of Parliament in certain cases
Power of President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament
Language to be used in Parliament

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 123 **of the** Indian Constitution** grants the** President the power to promulgate ordinances** when both houses of **Parliament **are not in session. 
 
• This power allows the** President to issue temporary laws that have the same effect as an Act of Parliament.** 
 
• These ordinances must be approved by **Parliament** within a specified period of time or they will cease to operate. 
 
• It's important to note that the **President's power to promulgate ordinances is not absolute and can be subject to certain limitations and conditions as prescribed by the Constitution.** 
 
• The ordinances must meet the requirements of immediate necessity and urgency, and they cannot be issued on matters that fall outside the legislative competence of Parliament.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **President of India**, as the** head of state and the constitutional head of the executive,** has various powers and functions outlined in the Indian Constitution. Some of the key powers of the President include:

 
 
• Executive Powers
 
• Legislative Powers
 
• Diplomatic Powers
 
• Emergency Powers
 
• Judicial Powers

__
 
• **The northern part **of the **Western Ghats** is also known as **Sahyadri.**
 
• **The Western Ghats **is a **mountain range** that runs **parallel to the western coast of the Indian subcontinent,** covering several states including **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Goa.**
 
• **The Sahyadri** name is commonly used to refer to the **northern part of the Western Ghats.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Range: **The Satpura Range is a mountain range located in **central** **India**.

 
 
• It extends across the states of **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh.**
 
• It is a **separate mountain range **with its own distinct geographical features.
 
 
 
• **Vindhya Range:** The Vindhya Range is a mountain range in central India, primarily located in the states of **Madhya Pradesh and Uttar** **Pradesh.**
 
 
• It runs parallel to the northern edge of the** Deccan Plateau**.
 
• It is a distinct mountain range separate from Sahyadri.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats: **The Western Ghats is a mountain range that runs parallel to the **western coast of the Indian subcontinent**.
 
 
• It extends from the state of **Gujarat in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south**.
 
• The Western Ghats are also known as **Sahyadri,** particularly the northern part of the range.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **and is known for its** rich biodiversity and numerous hill stations.**
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats:** The Eastern Ghats is a discontinuous **range of mountains along the eastern coast of India**.
 
 
• It stretches from **West Bengal in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south.**
 
• They have their own geographical characteristics and are known for their scenic beauty and important river systems.

questions.question: Which among the following pairs of rivers and tributaries is incorrect?

questions.question: The Indian Navy signed a contract of White Shipping Information Exchange to exchange information about the ships with the navy of ______ in October 2022.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The signing of a contract between **the Royal New Zealand Navy and the Indian Navy for the exchange of White Shipping Information Exchange (WSIE)** indicates a step towards **strengthening maritime cooperation and fostering openness in the maritime domain.**
 
• The agreement was signed by **Admiral R. Hari Kumar, Chief of Naval Staff of the Indian Navy, and Rear Admiral David Proctor, Chief of the New Zealand Navy.**
 
• **The White Shipping Information Exchange** is a mechanism that allows countries to share information about **commercial shipping in their respective regions.**

questions.question: Hydra is an example of which of the following phylum of the animal kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coelenterata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydra is an example of the phylum Coelenterata.**
 
• Coelenterates are a group of animals that have** radial symmetry, a gastrovascular cavity, and stinging cells called nematocysts.**
 
• Hydras are small, freshwater animals that have** cylindrical body with tentacles around their mouth.**
 
• **They feed on small animals that they capture with their tentacles.**
 
• **Hydras reproduce both sexually and asexually.**
 
• Hydras have radial symmetry, **which means that they have the same number of parts arranged around a central axis from any point.**
 
• Hydras have a gastrovascular cavity,** which is a single cavity that serves both for digestion and for circulation.**
 
• Hydras have stinging cells called **nematocysts, which they use to capture prey.**
 
• Hydras are small, freshwater animals.
 
• **Hydras reproduce both sexually and asexually.**

questions.question: Which among the following is a flat bone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flat bones are bones whose principal function is either extensive protection or the provision of broad surfaces for muscular attachment.**
 
• These bones are expanded into **broad, flat plates, as in the cranium (skull), the ilium (pelvis), sternum and the rib cage.**
 
• The ribs are a series of curved bones that attach to the spine in the back and to the sternum (breastbone) in the front.
 
• They form a cage around the** lungs and heart, protecting them from injury.**
 
• **The other options are not flat bones.**
 
 
• The ankle bones are called tarsals.
 
• They are small bones that form the ankle joint.
 
• The wrist bones are called carpals.
 
• They are small bones that form the wrist joint.
 
• The pelvic bones are called coxal bones.
 
• They are large bones that form the pelvis.
